A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, with proofs and architectures matchable despite reorganization and notation changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original experiments on quadratic optimization and training neural networks.

after.justification: Section 8 and Figures 1–2 retain original experimental results for both optimization tasks.

M1.justification: The learned updates, two-block architectures, training objective, progressive probabilistic constraint, and prior/posterior procedure remain unchanged. Figures 3–4 and the corresponding architecture appendices describe the same components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 200-dimensional quadratic problems and training a 351-parameter ReLU network on noisy polynomial regression problems. No additional dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Heavy-ball with friction remains the quadratic-problem comparator, and full-batch Adam remains the neural-network-training comparator. No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain unchanged, including the 500/250 trajectory horizons, Adam tuning and selected 0.008 step size, independent 500/500/250 function splits, and gradient-descent approximation of critical points.

E4.justification: Neither version reports additional empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, or robustness analyses. The new Appendix B contains mathematical counterexamples, assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Both retain mean/median curves and 95% test-data shading, plus quadratic evaluation on 250 test sets of 250 problems. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Plotted empirical estimates change under the same reported settings. For example, Figure 2's event-A estimate shifts from approximately 0.944 to 0.933, and Figure 1's probability estimates also shift slightly. The baseline rankings and stated approximately 75%/92% convergence bounds remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The main theorem is retained, but v2 adds two counterexamples concerning boundedness and relative error, and extends the measurability proof to general Polish state spaces. New Remark 7.7(iii) adds a bound approximation with an incorrect positive complexity term; the preceding theorem implies subtraction.

C1.justification: The central claim of high-probability convergence for learned optimization algorithms remains. Sections 1, 3, and 9 additionally claim applicability to Markovian sequential prediction models beyond optimization, modestly broadening the stated contribution.

C2.justification: Remark 6.6 and Appendix B explicitly explain why sufficient descent alone cannot guarantee convergence to a critical point. The conclusion also identifies sufficient descent as the obstacle to stochastic optimization. The four existing practical limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 8 newly provides a repository link for reproducing the results. Architecture, training, and data-split details in v1 Appendices E–G are retained in v2 Appendices G–I.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hellström et al. (2025), removes the broader meta-learning/AutoML discussion and the discussion of Xie et al. (2024), and sharpens its distinction from Sucker and Ochs (2024). Numerous publication and bibliographic updates concern the same cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. Dedicated Contributions and Simplified Key Idea sections reshape the narrative, notation and problem setup are separated, a main-text proof moves to an appendix, and terminology and mathematical notation are revised throughout.

P2.justification: All four figures remain, with revised sizing, labels, legends, captions, and placement. Plot titles are removed, histogram binning changes, and architecture diagrams are redrawn while retaining their components. No new figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: The new explanatory sections, counterexamples, and reproduction link improve accessibility and documentation. However, new Remark 7.7(iii) incorrectly adds rather than subtracts the complexity term, undermining its explanation of the central guarantee. The main theorem and experimental scope remain unchanged; the explanatory gains and newly introduced mathematical error leave the net quality direction uncertain.
